name: recency_stale_over_fresh
description: Timed hybrid-recall fixture: two ACTIVE claims compete as the answer for the same subject under a multi-valued predicate, so consolidation supersedes neither. Relevance alone cannot tell them apart, or mildly prefers the older one, and the stale claim takes the single result slot. Queries never name the expected object and no predicate or label says which claim is current.

queries.note: Exact score tie: both objects have the same tokens except the version, which the query omits. Hybrid recall breaks ties by ascending claim id, ids are time-ordered, so the 2025 claim wins over the 2026 one.

queries.query: what does the deploy-pipeline depend on
queries.note: Graph scores tie. The stale claim has the shorter text, so length normalisation gives it a slightly higher vector score.

envoy was written first and re-asserted in 2026-10, after nginx was written. nginx has the shorter text and the slightly higher vector score. Consolidation keeps the oldest envoy row and supersedes the re-assertion, so the surviving row carries only its 2025 timestamps: write time alone cannot rank it first.
Control: the query names the old object explicitly. Relevance must keep winning here whatever recency weight is used.
